speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand your condition, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and how high your fever has reached?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

Based on the classic presentation of a "slapped cheek" rash followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the extremities, along with the preceding flu-like prodrome, the clinical evidence strongly points to Parvovirus B19 infection. No further testing is required for this diagnosis.
